newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks little changed at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks little changed at midday.

text.p: Stocks retreated to nearly unchanged at midday Thursday as the technology sector, the engine behind the market's recent strength, paused for a breather.
Just after 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average, which hit a record high on Wednesday, was up 10.68 points to 8,269.99 after hitting a session high of 8,299.49 earlier in the day.
"We have come so far, so fast that this market is long overdue for a setback, or at least a rest," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"It's a non-starter market. We are in the plus column across the board, but I also see a lot of red on my screen," he said.
Advancing issues barely outpaced decliners on the New York Stock Exchange on a volume of 333 million shares.
The technology-laden Nasdaq composite index, which helped fuel the broader market's rise on Wednesday, gained 2.23 points to 1,632.67.
"We were very active to the upside this morning, but now people are waiting to see if the market comes in," said Jim Toth, head trader at McDonald & Co. "There's been a little break in the action."
Buoyant technology shares and a decline in bond yields gave new life to flagging blue chips on Wednesday and extended Nasdaq's string of record closes.
But with few fresh sparks in either of the markets Thursday, analysts said stocks paused.
"The market has gotten a bit frothy," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp. "I'd like to see a bit of a pause here."

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was marginally higher in quiet midday dealings as traders awaited the results of a $10 billion Treasury auction. The long bond rose 1/32, with its yield unchanged at 6.48 percent.

But while the stock market failed to make much headway Thursday, analysts said it remained broadly underpinned by a rosy U.S. economic outlook, solid corporate earnings results, benign inflation data and its own momentum.

"The market just keeps rolling," said Charles Pradilla, market analyst at Cowen & Co. "An incredible confluence of factors is really driving session after session -- a bond shortage, a budget deal, strong profits, low inflation..."
Among individual issues, SITEL Corp. fell 28 percent after several brokerage firms downgraded the stock, citing a lack of upside surprise in its second-quarter earnings. The stock lost 4-1/4 to 11.
Compaq Computer Corp. added 3-6/16 to 62-1/16 after Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette raised its rating on the stock.

United HealthCare Corp. slid 7-8/16 to 50-9/16. While it matched second- quarter earnings forecasts, it said lagging margins in several markets restrained growth and would likely be a drag on earnings for the rest of 1997.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks edged up eight-tenths of a point, to 961.13. The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.21 to 653.85.
